recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current core source change is needed for FHIR-15749 unless a future work group decision changes RequestPriority semantics or removes the action-level priority elements.
issue_request: FHIR-15749 was a Published/Persuasive CDS change request for STU3 asking to add a priority element to RequestGroup.action, with the same need called out for PlanDefinition.action.
initial_application: The request was applied in SVN/git import commit d366854435400372ecc374ea3bbf3330cfb854fa, which added RequestGroup.action.priority and PlanDefinition.action.priority rows with code type, RequestPriority binding, routine | urgent | asap | stat short text, and action-specific priority definitions.
additional_context: RequestGroup was later renamed to RequestOrchestration by FHIR-24619. Commit 46bea37a00e63d1ace04a5f322614c6d0815f500 carried RequestGroup.action.priority forward as RequestOrchestration.action.priority. source/fhir.ini lists PlanDefinition and RequestOrchestration as active resources, while RequestGroup appears only among deleted/legacy resource names. No Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active PlanDefinition and RequestOrchestration StructureDefinitions already contain 0..1 action.priority elements using code, the required http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/request-priority binding, and definitions indicating how quickly the action should be addressed with respect to other actions.

related_jiras.note: Renamed RequestGroup to RequestOrchestration and explains why the current active resource name differs from the original issue request.
